::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** April 21st 1874  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS John Rylands Library, Manchester, FA1/7/835
:::

My dear [Mr Freeman](people/person_523.qmd),
Many thanks for [King Ine](other_books/otherbook_845.qmd). I hope we are not to wait thirteen years for his second part.[^1]  It goes to my heart to lose St Boniface as a Devonshire man. What could have made them choose such a place for him to be born in as Crediton, if it was not true?  No wonder Ceadwalla was tempting to the Witch.!  I like Miss Macarthur’s [Scotland](other_books/otherbook_846.qmd) much, it keeps hold of a clear thread.[^2]

I have been catching it from the [Saturday](organizations/other_99.qmd) more than I have done for years!  I confess I thought it rather captious to blame me for not getting Sir John Elliot’s sufferings into [a baby history](cmy_books/cmybook_101.qmd) of 6 pages to each reign, and for saying the early times of Charles I were quiet, when I simply meant that there was not a civil war! Then there was a funny controversy between a correspondent of mine and the [Athenæum](organizations/other_170.qmd) critic as to whether Wat Tyler was on horseback or not as he appeared in the picture! Mr Kitchin’s [history of France](other_books/otherbook_847.qmd)seems to me very good as far as I have got, which is only to the Pippin times[^3]

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Edward Augustus Freeman, *King Ine* Part I (1872) and Part II (1874) were reprinted from the *Proceedings of the Somersetshire Archaeological and Natural History Society*.
[^2]: Margaret Macarthur, *History of Scotland* (London: Macmillan 1873), volume 3 of the Historical Course for Schools series edited by Freeman.
[^3]: The Rev. G. W. Kitchin's *A History of France* was published in three volumes between 1773-7.
